s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent pustular eruptions on the face with exacerbation by sunlight exposure
salient_findings: Recurrent pustular eruptions on the face
Failed response to broad-spectrum sunscreens, topical/oral antibiotics, and topical ivermectin
Intrafollicular and subcorneal pustule formation on histopathology
key_facts: 4-year history of recurrent pustular eruptions on the face
Eruptions initially occurred during a Florida vacation
Mild associated pruritus without burning sensation
Intermittent occurrence with erythematous papules and prominent pustules
Exacerbation by sunlight exposure, especially in summer months
Resolution within 3-4 days, leaving mild background erythema by 5-7 days
Failed response to broad-spectrum sunscreens, topical/oral antibiotics, and topical ivermectin
No joint pain, fever, fatigue, changes in urine color, medication use, or rashes elsewhere
No significant medical history
Numerous 1-2mm monomorphous pustules over background erythema on medial cheeks, chin, and nose
Negative serum antinuclear antibodies
Negative anti-SSA/Ro antibodies
Negative anti-SSB/La antibodies
Negative bacterial swab from malar lesions
Negative periodic acid–Schiff stain for fungal organisms
Negative Grocott methenamine silver stain for fungal organisms
Intrafollicular and subcorneal pustule formation on histopathology

shortlist.label: Polymorphic light eruption
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent pustular eruptions with exacerbation by sunlight exposure

shortlist.label: Subcorneal pustular dermatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Intrafollicular and subcorneal pustule formation on histopathology

shortlist.label: Eosinophilic pustular folliculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent pustular eruptions on the face with prominent pustules

shortlist.label: Pustular psoriasis
shortlist.why_kept: Pustular eruptions with background erythema, although lack of other psoriasis features

shortlist.label: Lupus miliaris disseminatus faciei
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent pustular eruptions on the face, although negative antinuclear antibodies

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of recurrent pustular eruptions on the face, exacerbation by sunlight exposure, and resolution within a few days are consistent with polymorphic light eruption. The initial occurrence during a Florida vacation and the lack of response to broad-spectrum sunscreens also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Subcorneal pustular dermatosis
rejected.why: While the histopathology shows subcorneal pustule formation, the clinical presentation and exacerbation by sunlight exposure are more characteristic of polymorphic light eruption.

rejected.label: Eosinophilic pustular folliculitis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and histopathology do not specifically suggest eosinophilic pustular folliculitis, and the lack of other characteristic features such as intense pruritus and follicular papules makes this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Pustular psoriasis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and histopathology do not show characteristic features of pustular psoriasis, such as widespread pustules and systemic symptoms, and the lack of response to topical/oral antibiotics and topical ivermectin does not support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Lupus miliaris disseminatus faciei
rejected.why: The patient's negative serum antinuclear antibodies, anti-SSA/Ro antibodies, and anti-SSB/La antibodies, as well as the lack of other characteristic features such as facial scarring and granulomatous histopathology, make this diagnosis unlikely.
